name: stocks-rag eval set - Videocon Industries Ltd (VIDEOIND), Q3 FY25 results
description: Hand-made test cases for POST /ask, written directly from the original PDF (not from the app's own output). Each case has the request to send, the ideal response, and simple checks to grade the real response.

document.units: Figures in Rs million unless stated. Brackets = negative (loss).

how_to_grade.must_contain: Every inner list is one required fact; the answer passes it if it contains ANY of the strings in that list (case-insensitive). All inner lists must pass.
how_to_grade.must_not_contain: None of these strings may appear (catches wrong columns / wrong numbers).
how_to_grade.expected_pages: At least one returned source must have one of these page values (sources[].pages can be a range like '1-2'; count it if the range covers the page).
how_to_grade.expect_not_found: true = the answer must be the not-found reply ('I could not find this in the ingested filings.') and must not invent a figure.
how_to_grade.calculated: true = the figure is NOT printed in the filing; the answer should derive it and say it is calculated.
how_to_grade.accept_any_of: For ambiguous questions: the answer passes if it matches any one listed interpretation AND states which period it used.
how_to_grade.needs_judge: true = deterministic checks are not enough on their own; an LLM judge should also review the answer (see judge_focus).

request.question: What was the net loss in Q1 FY25?

expected_response.answer: Calculated: (22,398.34) ₹ million. Nine months ended 31.12.2024 (71,401.31) [S1] minus quarter ended 30.09.2024 (24,104.41) [S1] minus quarter ended 31.12.2024 (24,898.56) [S1].

request.question: What was the revenue from operations in the first half of FY25?

expected_response.answer: Calculated: 3,278.54 ₹ million for H1 FY25 (six months ended 30.09.2024). Nine months ended 31.12.2024 revenue 4,855.51 [S1] minus quarter ended 31.12.2024 revenue 1,576.97 [S1].

cases.source_note: Not printed. 4,855.51 - 1,576.97 = 3,278.54. A model slip gave 3,240.69 in an earlier run.

request.question: What was the revenue from operations in Q1 FY25?

expected_response.answer: Calculated: 1,614.82 ₹ million. Nine months ended 31.12.2024 revenue 4,855.51 [S1] minus quarter ended 30.09.2024 1,663.72 [S1] minus quarter ended 31.12.2024 1,576.97 [S1].

request.question: By how much did finance costs increase from the September 2024 quarter to the December 2024 quarter?

expected_response.answer: Calculated: finance costs rose by 817.69 ₹ million, from 23,205.93 ₹ million (quarter ended 30.09.2024) to 24,023.62 ₹ million (quarter ended 31.12.2024) [S1].

request.question: What was the combined loss in the first three quarters of FY25?

expected_response.answer: (71,401.31) ₹ million - this is printed as the loss for the nine months ended 31.12.2024, which covers Q1+Q2+Q3 FY25 [S1].

request.question: What was the loss for the last 6 months?

expected_response.answer: Calculated, taking the last 6 months as Q2 + Q3 FY25 (1 Jul to 31 Dec 2024): (24,104.41) + (24,898.56) = (49,002.97) ₹ million [S1].

request.question: Since when has trading in the company's shares been suspended?

expected_response.answer: Trading in the company's securities has been suspended on BSE and NSE since June 16, 2021 [S1].

cases.source_note: Cover letter, page 1

request.question: Who is the Resolution Professional of the company?

expected_response.answer: Mr. Abhijit Guhathakurta is the Resolution Professional for the 13 Videocon Group Entities, including the company [S1].

cases.source_note: Cover letter p1-2, auditor report p5 (c), notes p12 c)

request.question: When was the insolvency process (CIRP) against the company admitted, and who was first appointed as resolution professional?

expected_response.answer: NCLT Mumbai admitted the CIRP application (under Section 7 of the IBC) by an order dated June 6, 2018, and appointed Mr. Anuj Jain as the insolvency resolution professional [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 2(a) p4; notes a) p12

request.question: Whose resolution plan did the Committee of Creditors approve, and with what voting share?

expected_response.answer: The CoC approved the resolution plan submitted by Twin Star Technologies Limited with a 95.09% majority voting share [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 2(d) p5; notes d) p12

request.question: Which tribunal stayed the NCLT order approving the resolution plan, and on what date?

expected_response.answer: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), New Delhi stayed the operation of the NCLT Approval Order by its order dated July 19, 2021 [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 2(f) p5; notes e) p12. Sensitive to the NCLT/NCLAT transcription errors seen earlier.

request.question: What happened to the NCLT approval of the resolution plan in January 2022?

expected_response.answer: By its final order dated January 05, 2022, the NCLAT set aside the Approval Order and sent the matter back to the CoC to complete the CIRP; the CoC then decided on January 12, 2022 to invite fresh expressions of interest [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 2(f)-(g) p5; notes e) p12

request.question: What are the Supreme Court civil appeal numbers filed by Twin Star Technologies?

expected_response.answer: Twin Star Technologies challenged the NCLAT Final Order in Civil Appeals numbers 509, 512 and 894 of 2022 before the Supreme Court [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 2(h) p6 (OCR page); notes f) p12

request.question: Who is the statutory auditor and what kind of conclusion did they give on these results?

expected_response.answer: The auditor, GAMP & Co., Chartered Accountants, issued a Disclaimer of Conclusion: they could not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence, so they did not express a conclusion on the Statement [S1][S2].

cases.source_note: Auditor letterhead p4; para 3 p6; para 6 p10

request.question: Who audited the previous period's figures and what opinion did they give?

expected_response.answer: The predecessor auditor, M/s KVA & Company, reviewed/audited the corresponding figures (quarter and nine months ended 31.12.2023 and year ended 31.03.2024) and expressed a Disclaimer of Opinion [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report para 7 Other Matters, p10 (OCR page)

request.question: Why were these financial results submitted late?

expected_response.answer: Because of the ongoing CIRP and related constraints: resignation of key accounting personnel, non-availability of pre-CIRP records, lack of cooperation from the promoters and erstwhile management, and the change of auditor [S1].

cases.source_note: Cover letter p1

request.question: What is the Ravva Oil and Gas Field and how were its figures included?

expected_response.answer: Ravva Oil and Gas Field is an unincorporated joint venture. Its figures were included based on information provided by the Operator / Joint Venture and were not independently audited or reviewed for the quarter [S1].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 5(s) p9

request.question: What business segments does the company operate in?

expected_response.answer: Two segments: (i) Consumer Electronics & Home Appliances (including rental income from assets) and (ii) Oil & Natural Gas [S1].

cases.source_note: Note xiii) p13; segment table p12

request.question: Is there any doubt about the company continuing as a going concern?

expected_response.answer: Yes. The auditor reports a material uncertainty about the company's ability to continue as a going concern: operations have declined, net worth is negative, losses continue and it is a co-obligor on other borrowers' loans; it depends on the resolution plan. The results are still prepared on a going concern basis because the company is run as a going concern under CIRP [S1][S2].

cases.source_note: Auditor report 5(p) p9; note vii) p13

request.question: On what date did the Resolution Professional sign the financial results, given there was no board meeting?

expected_response.answer: The Resolution Professional signed the financials on 10 February 2026; no board meeting was held because the board's powers are vested in the RP under the IBC [S1].

cases.source_note: Cover letter p2; signature block p13

request.question: How many Videocon group companies are in the consolidated insolvency process?

expected_response.answer: 13 companies: Videocon Industries Limited together with 12 other Videocon group companies (the 'Videocon Group Entities') [S1].

cases.source_note: Cover letter p1 ('12 other'), p2 ('13 Videocon Group Companies'); auditor report p4-5
